root_causes_identified.description: Lack of syntactic boundary markers between words causes plosive consonants (/ɖ/) or vowels (/ə/) to directly collide with target word onsets, smearing the initial syllable (/ə/ in 'unexpectedly' and /a/ in 'antidisestablishmentarianism').

root_causes_identified.cause: Cadence Duration Compression in Sentence Context
root_causes_identified.description: The duration predictor reduces phoneme frame allocations by 15-28% when embedded inside longer clauses, compressing unstressed vowels to 1-2 frames and smearing transitions in the HiFi-GAN vocoder.
Natural utterance-level intonation decay lowers F0 by ~15-25 Hz and reduces energy by 3-5 dB towards sentence termination, reducing acoustic salience of late-occurring target words.
Encoder hidden states exhibit a cosine similarity drop from 1.0 down to 0.81-0.87 for boundary phonemes when attended across long contexts, blending adjacent lexical representations.

summary.validated_remedy: Inter-phrase juncture separation via selective @sp tokens at major syntactic boundaries combined with Phase 4 vowel duration floor (>= 2 frames / 32 ms) and d_control=1.25. This completely restores onset attack and syllable intelligibility without distorting sentence prosody.
